Investigation Findings & Root Cause Analysis

  1. Terminal vs App Execution Overhead:

    • Direct standalone pano.exe runs isolated binary logic without external event overhead:
      • Direct terminal: ~12.48s for 4-photo fullframe fisheye at 4K resolution (Create: 3.06s, Render: 9.41s).
      • App Production Pipeline: ~11.88s - 17.34s for 4-photo stitching at 4K resolution.
    • The execution delta (+1.27x to +1.48x total elapsed time in the app) is driven entirely by orchestration overhead rather than engine degradation:
      • Tauri IPC & Async Task Scheduling: stitching_start_queue dispatches through tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking.
      • Two-Way HS1 Handshake Protection: spawn_with_handshake launches pano.exe and performs process verification over pipe channels before execution.
      • Per-Job Scratch Filesystem Cleanup: Temporary project directories (scratch) are dynamically allocated, sanitized, and wiped per panorama.
      • Real-Time Webview Event Streaming: Frequent progress updates (stitching-progress & stitching-log-update) and in-memory queue state updates are emitted to the React renderer every 100ms-1500ms.
      • Post-Render Dimension & Metadata Extraction: Reading output resolution from physical disk before marking status as Success.

  2. Resolution & Size Correlation:

    • Fixed app overhead is relatively constant (~5-10 seconds). Therefore, for smaller output sizes (4K), relative overhead appears higher (~1.48x), whereas for high-resolution outputs (8K, 12K, Auto), the ratio drops to ~1.27x-1.32x as raw rendering compute dominates execution time.

issues.display_title: Issue #245: feat(image-to-video): Implement Google Veo 3.1 2-Frame Interpolation Video Generator
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Summary & Objective

Implement the Google Veo 3.1 image-to-video generation pipeline in Photo Studio (Edit → Image to Video). This enables users to generate high-fidelity cinematic video walkthroughs from an equirectangular 360 panorama using Start and End rectilinear frame interpolation and standardized cinematic camera movements.

Related PRD: #243 ([PRD] Editor Image to Video Generator)

Key Capabilities & Scope

1. Frame Selection & Alignment (2-Frame Interpolation)

  • Equirectangular Source Loading: Select 360 image from browser or drag-and-drop.
  • Start Frame & End Frame Capture: Capture rectilinear stills (ipc.eq2photoCapture) directly from the 360 viewer.
  • Angle Constraints & Orbit Limits: Limit the End Frame yaw and pitch to ±45°/±90° relative to the Start Frame orientation to ensure smooth visual transition without severe perspective distortion.
  • Aspect Ratio Locking: Support 16:9 (horizontal) and 9:16 (vertical) formats, locking the selection once the Start Frame is chosen.
  • Frame Management: Visual preview cards for Start & End frames with one-click removal and cascade clearing.

2. Camera Movements & Motion Prompts

  • Curated Movement Library: 39 cinematic camera movements categorized under:
    • Pan/Tilt (Pan Right/Left, Whip Pan, Tilt Up/Down)
    • Zoom/Lens (Slow/Fast/Crash Zoom In/Out, Infinite Zoom, Tilt Shift)
    • Dolly/Track (Dolly In/Out, Tracking Shot, Follow, Reverse/Side/Low Tracking)
    • Physical Moves (Truck, Pedestal, Slider, Push Past, Arc, Orbit)
    • Human Camera (Handheld, Body-mounted, First-person view)
    • Drone/Crane (Crane Up/Down, Drone Push/Pull, Helicopter)
    • Specials (Time-lapse, Pass Through Objects, Earth Zoom Out)
  • Prompt Synthesizer: Formats shot description and integrates optional custom user prompt (≤ 2,000 chars limit).

3. Backend Generation Engine (src-tauri/src/commands/image_to_video.rs)

  • Google Gemini Veo API Integration:
    • Endpoint: POST {BASE_URL}/models/veo-3.1-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
    • Headers: x-goog-api-key: {apiKey}
    • Payload structure: 
      {
  "instances": [{
    "prompt": "{formatted_prompt}",
    "image": { "bytesBase64Encoded": "{b64_start}", "mimeType": "image/jpeg" },
    "lastFrame": { "bytesBase64Encoded": "{b64_end}", "mimeType": "image/jpeg" }
  }],
  "parameters": {
    "aspectRatio": "16:9" | "9:16",
    "durationSeconds": 8,
    "resolution": "720p",
    "sampleCount": 1
  }
}
  • Asynchronous Polling:
    • Poll GET {BASE_URL}/{operation_name} with exponential backoff / 10s interval (15-minute timeout).
    • Safety filter handling (raiMediaFilteredReasons).
  • Download & Persistence:
    • Stream/download generated MP4 from Google Storage sample URI.
    • Automatically create target folder ({source_dir}/image-to-video/) and write video file with timestamped naming.

4. UI/UX & Feedback

  • Shared GeneralsTab API key integration (filtered to Google AI keys).
  • Generation state handling (Idle, Ready, Generating spinner, Success, Failed).
  • Toast alerts (react-toastify) and "View" button to reveal generated MP4 in OS file manager.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Users can capture Start Frame and End Frame from equirectangular panorama.
  • Aspect ratio (16:9 and 9:16) locks consistently across both frames.
  • Camera movement dropdown lists all 39 presets and enforces selection.
  • Optional prompt textarea enforces ≤ 2,000 character limit.
  • Backend sends valid Veo 3.1 predictLongRunning request and polls until completion.
  • Output MP4 is saved to {source_dir}/image-to-video/ and can be opened in OS file explorer.
  • All user-facing strings localized in src/locales/*.json.
  • Typecheck (pnpm typecheck) and Rust check (cargo check) pass cleanly.

DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Summary & Objective

Implement the Gemini Omni trajectory-guided image-to-video generation pipeline in Photo Studio (Edit → Image to Video). This allows users to direct camera walkthroughs, curves, and turns by interactively drawing camera paths on the preview image, synthesizing motion trajectories for the AI video generator.

Related PRD: #243 ([PRD] Editor Image to Video Generator)

Key Capabilities & Scope

1. Interactive Trajectory Drawing Canvas (TrajectoryCanvas.tsx)

  • Direct Canvas Interaction: Interactive vector drawing overlay positioned over the Start Frame preview.
  • Touch / Mouse Drawing: Captures freeform cursor coordinates normalized to 0–100% canvas bounds.
  • Dynamic Bézier Curve Smoothing: Implements pointsToSvgPath converting raw sample points into smooth quadratic Bézier curves (Q / L SVG path commands).
  • Visual Path Styling:
    • Vibrant directional gradient stroke (omniCurveGrad) indicating start-to-finish flow.
    • Marker arrowhead (omniCurveArrow) displaying heading direction.
    • Waypoint node anchors and active drawing feedback.
  • Canvas State Controls: Reset/Clear action, path redraw, and generation-lock responsiveness.

2. Trajectory Analysis & Prompt Translation Engine (trajectoryUtils.ts)

  • Ramer-Douglas-Peucker (RDP) Algorithm: Simplifies raw dense path points into key directional waypoints (epsilon filtering).
  • Kinematic & Angle Analysis:
    • Calculates Euclidean distance and path segment angles in screen space.
    • Computes deltaYaw (turning degrees) and forwardProgress (zoom/dolly forward depth).
    • Classifies trajectories into intuitive motions: Straight Walk, Soft Right Turn, Sharp Left Turn, S-Curve Walkthrough, Lateral Arc.
  • Natural Language Translation: Converts vector path data into descriptive natural language prompts fed to the model (e.g., Walk forward into the room, gently curving to the right...).

3. Single-Frame & Dual-Pano Walkthrough Flexibility

  • Single-Frame Trajectory Walkthrough: Generate video from a single Start Frame driven exclusively by the drawn camera path.
  • Optional End Frame Anchor:
    • Toggle switch "Include End Frame" in Omni mode.
    • Auto-synthesizes destination End Frame based on computed trajectory deltaYaw and forward FOV zoom.
  • Dual-Panorama Navigation: Support switching between Start Panorama and End Panorama (activeViewerTarget) when creating walkthrough transitions between two different camera positions.

4. Backend Omni Integration (src-tauri/src/commands/image_to_video.rs)

  • Extend backend image_to_video_generate command to support the omni engine variant.
  • Parse engine: "omni", trajectory prompt metadata, and optional End Frame.
  • Call Gemini Omni video generation endpoint with appropriate payload formatting.
  • Handle long-running task polling, rate limits, and output video persistence.

5. UI/UX & Engine Switching

  • Engine switcher tab (Google Veo 3.1 vs Gemini Omni) in Settings.tsx.
  • Trajectory overview card displaying movement classification, icon, and step count.
  • Contextual guidance hints guiding users through drawing, clearing, and generating.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Users can smoothly draw camera trajectories on the preview canvas with real-time SVG curve and arrowhead feedback.
  • Trajectory analysis accurately classifies camera motion and generates natural language movement prompts.
  • "Clear" button resets drawn path and restores ready state.
  • Toggle for "Include End Frame" correctly enables/disables destination frame anchoring.
  • Dual-panorama mode allows selecting a separate end panorama and framing its perspective.
  • Backend supports omni engine request assembly and artifact retrieval.
  • UI seamlessly switches between Veo (camera movements dropdown) and Omni (trajectory canvas).
  • All user-facing strings localized in src/locales/*.json.
  • Typecheck (pnpm typecheck) and Rust check (cargo check) pass cleanly.

Fix Capture Photo on Preview

Summary

Capture Photo in Preview should export a flat (rectilinear) JPEG from the current 360° viewer angle using the bundled eq2photo binary. The renderer flow is already implemented, but the Tauri backend command is missing, so capture either fails silently or never becomes available in the UI.

Problem

Expected behavior (Electron parity): In Preview, when viewing a panorama in Normal mode, the camera button captures the current view and writes gothru_capture_<timestamp>.jpg to the active folder. The user sees loading state, success/failure toast, a log entry with preview link, and a processing-file row (uploadTo: 'capture').

Current behavior:

Layer Status
Renderer (Preview/Main.tsx) Implemented — handleCapture, FOV/angle conversion, toast, logs, processing UI
Bridge (electron-bridge.ts) Mapped — eq2photoCapture → eq2photo-capture
Binaries Present — src-tauri/binaries/mac/eq2photo, win/eq2photo.exe
Rust backend Missing — no eq2photo.rs, command not registered in lib.rs
IPC inventory Still unported — eq2photo-capture is one of the 2 remaining channels

User-visible symptoms:

  1. Capture button may not appear — button only renders when normal && isPanorama && !isVideo. Incorrect panorama detection hides it.

  3. Silent no-op — handleCapture exits early if panoramaViewStateRef or panoramaViewSizeRef is still null (viewer state not yet reported).
  4. Angle parity risk — output must match Electron exactly: vertical→horizontal FOV, yawDeg = -(yaw - 90), pitchDeg = -(pitch - 90). Wrong convention = wrong crop.

UI / UX

  • Loading state on button during capture
  • Success/failure toast + log entry with previewFilePath on success
  • Processing file row appears with uploadTo: 'capture'

Parity (severity: H)

Description

A critical performance bug was reported by a user attempting to process a very large batch of images (4,536 images) using the Enfuse feature.

Issue Details

  1. The user initiated an enfuse job for the entire batch.
  2. The processing engine successfully enfused the very first image and saved it to disk.
  3. However, the app's Queue UI failed to update (Success counter stayed at 0, and the item stayed stuck on Queued).
  4. The entire application became completely unresponsive - none of the interactive UI buttons worked, forcing the user to force-quit the app.
  5. Visual feedback (the rotating blue loading indicator) kept looping, indicating the UI thread is locked or overwhelmed without technically crashing the OS window.

This strongly indicates the heavy image processing is either blocking the main/UI thread, causing a memory issue when loading thousands of file paths, or the queue manager is failing to catch the success callback from the processing engine to trigger the next item.

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md (section 3 Edit suite / section 8): Enfuse is a native-binary-backed batch Edit tool. Same family as the other queue/throughput issues - see #1407 (AutoLevel slow save: strictly-sequential queue, per-file process churn). At 4,536 items the queue/state model likely degrades non-linearly.

Investigation directions

  • UI-thread blocking: ensure batch orchestration + per-item state updates are not synchronously processing the full 4.5k list on the renderer/main thread; yield/stream instead of building giant arrays.
  • Success callback wiring: confirm the per-item success event from the Enfuse engine actually updates the queue (counter + status) and triggers the next item - the "1 done but counter=0/Queued" symptom points here.
  • Memory: loading thousands of file paths/objects at once - paginate/virtualize the queue list; avoid retaining buffers.
  • Responsiveness: Stop All / Cancel must stay clickable (don't block the event loop); process incrementally.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The application can successfully queue and process massive batches (e.g. 5,000 images) without locking up the UI.
  2. Interactive elements (especially Stop All / Cancel) remain fully clickable and responsive while a heavy batch job runs in the background.
  3. The queue accurately updates the Success counter and visual status for each item as soon as it is written to disk.

Description

A highly disruptive UX issue has been reported within the Enfuse feature. Whenever a user performs an action that updates the list-specifically adding a new image or deleting an existing image-the UI forcibly resets the user's scroll position to the very top of the page.

This causes severe friction for users working with large datasets. For example, a user managing a massive batch job with 15,000 images reported extreme frustration, as they have to manually scroll all the way back down to their previous location after every single deletion.

}, []);
